description: Company profiles. A company never replaces the role baseline - it modifies it. focus_skills raise (or promote) skills the company screens hardest for, keywords feed the ATS and keyword-similarity stages, and values feed the soft-signal checks.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.tagline: Scale, ownership and measurable customer impact.
hiring_signals: Bullets that quantify impact - Amazon interviews are built around the STAR format and metrics
Evidence you owned something end to end rather than contributed to it
Familiarity with AWS services relevant to the role, named explicitly
companies.screen_notes: Amazon's bar raiser process weights Leadership Principles as heavily as technical depth. Resume bullets that read as team accomplishments without a personal contribution tend to screen poorly.

companies.name: Google
companies.tagline: Algorithmic depth and systems that work at planetary scale.
hiring_signals: Explicit algorithmic and complexity vocabulary in project descriptions
Open-source contributions, publications or competitive programming records
Depth in one area rather than a long shallow tool list
companies.screen_notes: Google screens heavily on fundamentals. A resume packed with frameworks but thin on data structures, algorithms or systems reasoning often stalls at the recruiter stage.

companies.name: Microsoft
hiring_signals: Evidence of learning new technologies quickly - the growth-mindset signal
Cross-team collaboration described concretely
Azure services named where they were genuinely used
companies.screen_notes: Microsoft values breadth plus collaboration signals. Resumes that show only solo work can read as a partnership risk for enterprise teams.

companies.name: Meta
companies.tagline: Move fast on products used by billions, backed by data.
hiring_signals: Impact stated in user or business terms, not just technical output
Experimentation and metric movement described numerically
Comfort with ambiguity and fast iteration
companies.screen_notes: Meta screens for impact per unit time. Bullets that describe tasks rather than outcomes are the most common weakness in candidate resumes.

companies.name: Apple
companies.tagline: Craft, privacy and deep ownership of a small surface done perfectly.
hiring_signals: Depth and polish on a small number of projects rather than many shallow ones
Performance, memory or latency work described concretely
Privacy-conscious or on-device engineering experience
companies.screen_notes: Apple hires specialists. A generalist resume with no clearly deepest area is the most common mismatch.

companies.name: Netflix
companies.tagline: Senior-heavy teams, high freedom, high responsibility, streaming scale.
hiring_signals: Evidence of operating autonomously without heavy process
Experience at meaningful scale or with resilience engineering
Strong written communication - Netflix runs on memos
companies.screen_notes: Netflix hires few, senior people. Early-career resumes need exceptional depth or scale signals to clear the bar.

companies.name: IBM
companies.tagline: Enterprise, hybrid cloud and applied AI for regulated industries.
hiring_signals: Client or stakeholder-facing experience described explicitly
Certifications carry more weight here than at most product companies
Governance, compliance or reliability awareness
companies.screen_notes: IBM roles are often client-facing. Consulting, documentation and certification signals move the needle more than at pure product companies.

companies.name: Adobe
companies.tagline: Creative tooling, applied AI and pixel-level product craft.
hiring_signals: Portfolio-quality projects with visible output
Generative or vision work applied to real creative problems
Close collaboration with design described concretely
companies.screen_notes: Adobe likes evidence you can make something people enjoy using. Screenshots, demos and links carry real weight.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.tagline: Accelerated computing - performance is the product.
hiring_signals: Measured speedups and benchmark numbers
Low-level performance work in C++, CUDA or Triton
Understanding of hardware constraints behind ML workloads
companies.screen_notes: NVIDIA screens for performance engineering. ML resumes with no systems or optimisation content are a common mismatch even when the ML is strong.
